summary: Phase B11+ regression testing (superadmin router split + event bus emitters + WebSocket live cockpit). 28/28 backend pytest cases PASS + frontend smoke PASS. Verified: (1) 20-route sampling across the 7 split sub-routers all reachable; (2) byte-identical dashboard (total=4194.63, scope1=251.86); (3) /api/health/contracts modules_checked>=22, failed=[]; (4) event_bus.handler_count = 1 for AUDIT_PERSISTED, EMISSION_SAVED, EMISSION_UPDATED, EMISSION_DELETED; (5) WebSocket /api/ws/dashboard rejects missing/invalid token (close 1008), accepts valid JWT with hello frame, replies to ping with pong; (6) POST /api/emissions broadcasts both dashboard.refresh{reason:emission.changed} + dashboard.refresh{reason:audit.persisted}; DELETE produces the same two events; (7) org-isolation enforced — super_admin WS receives org A's event while org B WS does NOT; (8) frontend login -> /dashboard renders [data-testid='dashboard-scope123'], WS handshake completes (hello frame visible in page WS frames), [data-testid='dashboard-live-badge'] correctly absent on first load.

issues: Minor: TWO WebSocket connections are opened on dashboard mount (observed 2 'WS opened' events with identical token in Playwright). Likely React.StrictMode double-effect in dev OR a cleanup-then-remount race in useDashboardLiveStream.js. Functionally harmless (both receive hello, backend disconnects the older one when component re-renders) but doubles connection count and audit churn. Worth checking the effect dependency array / abort cleanup in /app/frontend/src/pages/dashboard/useDashboardLiveStream.js.

critical_code_review_comments: [POSITIVE — router split done correctly] modules/superadmin/router.py reduced from 2502 -> 22 lines (aggregator only). The 7 sub-routers are sized 228-571 lines each, all under the 700-line guideline. No NameError leakage on the routes I sampled. GWP_VALUES correctly retained where needed.

[POSITIVE — event bus wiring is idempotent] ws_router.py registers handlers at module import via event_bus.subscribe. Handler count stays at exactly 1 per event after multiple test imports; the bus uses a set under the hood — good.

[POSITIVE — WS auth is correct] Token parsed from query string, JWT verified with shared JWT_SECRET/JWT_ALGORITHM, user looked up in db.users, deleted_at and status checks both enforced. Connection closed with 1008 before .accept() when invalid — proper protocol behavior.

[POSITIVE — org filter logic] broadcast() short-circuits org-mismatched non-super_admin clients before send_text, so org B can't even observe org A events on the wire. Snapshotted set before iterating to avoid mutation-during-iteration.

[MINOR — frontend hook double-connect] Two WS connections opened on dashboard mount in Playwright (same JWT, both got hello). Suspect React StrictMode dev double-effect OR missing abort cleanup in useDashboardLiveStream.js useEffect. In production build the impact may be zero, but worth verifying the cleanup function actually closes the previous ws before opening a new one.

[MINOR — WS message protocol could be tighter] Server happily accepts any non-JSON text frame and silently continues; consider closing on N invalid frames or rate-limiting pings to defend against misbehaving clients.

[MINOR — broadcast() dead-client GC under lock] manager.broadcast iterates over a list snapshot but calls self.remove (which takes the lock) inside the loop after collecting `dead`. Fine functionally; could be slightly more efficient by removing under one lock acquisition.
[INFO] passlib bcrypt AttributeError warning in backend logs is a known passlib<>bcrypt 5.x compat issue — does not affect auth. Pre-existing.
